name: MAXS Door Handler
author: Ari Tsironis

provenance.from: AMOSTools/Extensions, out of aminet dev/amos/amostools.i386-aros.lha -- held in the corpus at sources/aminet-dev-amos/. Its author's README says the directory is "every AMOS extension I can find, cut down to just their token tables with the make_extensions.pl script", and names the ExoticA AMOS extensions wiki page as the list it works from.
provenance.redistribution: Not redistributed here as software: the file carries no code at all. It is a token table with the library stripped out from under it, kept for identification and detokenising.
provenance.note: ExoticA's AMOS extensions list places it at slot 16. Nothing here observes it in a program: the slot is the wiki's recommendation and no more.

notes: TABLE ONLY. This is an AMOSTools stub -- the hunk shell and the token table survive, both length fields read zero, there is no code, and every entry's two routine words are overwritten with `====`. So the NAMES, the parameter SPECS and, because an id is the byte offset of its entry, the IDS are the original library's; the behaviour is not here and the evidence tier cannot rise above `manual` until a real binary turns up. The reader is checked against CRAFT and MusiCRAFT, which are held both ways, and agrees with them entry for entry -- see parseAmosToolsTable in src/tokens/libtok.ts. 21 keywords, all prefixed `m_` and none contested -- a BBS door API for the MAXS bulletin board: `m_portopen`/`m_portclose`, three character readers (`m_modemchar`, `m_screenchar`, `m_bbschar`), text out to the caller or the sysop console (`m_bbstext`, `m_localtext`), prompts, file show/check/edit, and the user record (`m_getusernum`, `m_getuserstr`, `m_newaccess`, `m_addtime`, `m_changeuserdata`, `m_twituser`). The naming is C-style throughout, which no other AMOS extension here does.
